Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side. Please reply if I missed anything.

Key performance / SLO items you called out:
- Latency (p95): target <150ms for US customer-facing flows, <220ms EU, <300ms APAC for API responses (streaming allowed).
- Throughput: steady-state ~120 req/s, occasional spikes to ~500 req/s for batch jobs.
- Concurrency: expect up to ~8 concurrent requests per user/session; overall concurrency budget ~400-600 concurrent connections.
- Streaming: required for long-form assistant responses and transcripts — we need end-to-end streaming with chunked tokens.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU regions; APAC pilot requires data to be in apac region when serving APAC users.

Questions / clarifications for Finova:
1) Are the latency targets strict SLOs for GA or initial GA+3 months?
2) Typical payload sizes (avg tokens per request / response) and percent of streaming vs non-streaming requests?
3) Any strict IP allowlist / VPC peering requirements for EU residency?

Next steps (owner):
- Aditya (SE) to follow up with recommended regional routing and autoscale config and list of network ports/ips we’ll need (by EOD Fri).
- Marissa to send SLO matrix + network diagram (attached) and propose tech deep-dive times.
- Finova to share typical payload sizes and any procurement timelines.

Attachments: redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO/throughput assumptions), network-routing-diagram.pdf

Thanks —

Marissa —

Thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 150ms p95 is our ideal for the US search experience; for initial pilot we can tolerate up to 200ms p95 while we validate the model config. Production GA target is 150ms.
- Typical payloads: requests average ~120 tokens, responses ~450 tokens. About 35% of our requests need streaming (live transcripts + tokens).
- Traffic split: roughly 55% US, 30% EU, 15% APAC. For EU it’s critical that customer PII and any transcripts stay in EU region.
- Current infra: GCP us-east1 (primary), europe-west1 (replica), APAC is currently on-prem in SG for pilot. We will need either VPC peering or a PrivateLink-style option for the EU residency case.

Open items for Redwood:
1) Can routing be geo-aware with sticky regional routing so EU traffic hits EU-only nodes for data residency?
2) What are the streaming latency expectations for chunked token delivery (we need <50ms token-chunk latency once streaming starts)?
3) If we use Dedicated capacity, can we pin model versions across regions to avoid warmup jitter during failover?

We can share our security questionnaire and procurement timeline by Monday. Also looping in procurement on this thread (procurement@finova.com).

—Samir
VP Product, Finova

Subject: Re: Finova - Performance SLO & Regional Routing - post-call follow-up

Samir — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. A few technical notes and proposals based on the numbers you provided:

1) Geo-aware sticky routing: yes — we support routing policies that prefer regional pools (us/eu/apac) and honor residency by routing reads/writes to region-scoped Dedicated pools. Fallback: if EU pool is overloaded we can failover to EU-compatible variants (quantized models) in the same region or to a warmed standby in eu-west1.

2) Latency/streaming: with streaming enabled our runtime pushes token chunks as soon as they are generated. In practice we see sub-50ms per-chunk delivery on warm paths for standard networks; cold starts / first-token may be higher. For strict token-chunk p95 <50ms we recommend: pinned model replicas, aggressive warm pools (min_replicas=2 per region), and direct peering to reduce network hops.

3) Throughput/concurrency: given ~120 req/s steady and peaks to 500 req/s, we recommend Dedicated capacity with autoscale profiles that trigger by sustained CPU/GPU utilization and queue-depth thresholds. For concurrency, we typically size replicas to handle ~8 concurrent requests (depending on model size); we can provide an initial sizing matrix if you share model variant and average sequence lengths.

4) KV / prefix caching: for multi-region consistency we recommend regional KV caches with a short TTL for cross-region reads; since you want EU residency, any cached PII should be region-bound and we can configure cache keys to include region scope.

5) Networking: we’ll send a short IP/port allowlist and recommended VPC peering guidance in the follow-up doc. For on-prem APAC gateway we can support private endpoints + TLS mutual auth.

Next actions from my side: I’ll draft a recommended Dedicated sizing + routing policy (with warm pool settings) and a checklist of network artifacts we’ll need. Target: EOD Friday.

—Aditya
